items.text: Wash hands and don PPE if appropriate
Introduce yourself including your name and role
Confirm the patient's identity
Explain the examination and gain consent
Position the patient at 45 degrees
Ensure adequate exposure while maintaining dignity
Inspect the patient from the end of the bed for breathlessness, pain, or distress
Look for signs of cardiac failure (orthopnoea, oedema, cyanosis)
Note any medications, oxygen, or monitoring equipment
Inspect hands for clubbing, splinter haemorrhages, Osler nodes, or Janeway lesions
Check peripheral temperature and capillary refill
Palpate radial pulse rate, rhythm, and character
Measure blood pressure in both arms if indicated
Inspect eyes for anaemia, jaundice, xanthelasma, or corneal arcus
Inspect mouth for dental disease or high-arched palate
Assess jugular venous pressure at 45 degrees
Palpate carotid pulses and auscultate for bruits
Inspect the precordium for scars, visible apex beat, or pulsations
Palpate the apex beat and assess character
Palpate for heaves or thrills
Auscultate over all four cardiac areas with the diaphragm
Auscultate with the bell at the apex for low-pitched murmurs
Listen for radiation of murmurs to the neck or axilla if a murmur is heard
Auscultate lung bases for bibasal crackles
Inspect legs for peripheral oedema
Palpate the abdomen for hepatomegaly if heart failure suspected
Assess for sacral oedema if the patient can lie flat
Check for ankle or sacral pressure areas
Thank the patient and restore clothing
Summarise examination findings to the examiner or patient
